overview: A group-level QI project using the Model for Improvement: a 12-week retrospective weekly baseline from the report builder, then four PDSA cycles of about four weeks each that introduce and refine the prescribing prompt, the consult-room guide, free urine culture and monthly clinic feedback.
population: All systemic antimicrobial prescriptions for dogs and cats in the four clinics from July 2026 to January 2027; topical and ophthalmic products are excluded.
exposure: Change package: a prompt when an HPCIA is selected (culture result or a reason from a pick-list plus free text), a one-page guide in each consult room, free in-house urine culture for suspected cystitis in October and November, nurse tablet-giving appointments for cat owners, and a monthly anonymised feedback email with each clinic's HPCIA share against the group.
procedures: Cycle 1 (October): prompt and guide in the two clinics with the highest baseline share. Cycle 2 (November): all four clinics, prompt reasons reviewed and the pick-list revised. Cycle 3 (December): nurse tablet-giving appointments added. Cycle 4 (January): feedback continues after free culture ends. The practice manager runs the weekly report every Monday; the head nurse samples 30 urinary consultations per clinic each month by hand.

outcomes.name: HPCIA share
outcomes.measure: Weekly number of systemic antimicrobial prescriptions that are HPCIAs (third-generation cephalosporins including cefovecin, fluoroquinolones, polymyxins) divided by all systemic antimicrobial prescriptions for dogs and cats, from the report builder
outcomes.why: Directly measures the prescribing the guideline restricts and is extractable without reading notes (claim c3).

outcomes.name: Culture before treatment for urinary signs
outcomes.measure: Monthly manual sample of 30 consultations per clinic with lower urinary tract signs: proportion with a urine culture submitted before any antimicrobial
outcomes.why: Shows whether the free culture change was used.

outcomes.name: Prompt reasons recorded
outcomes.measure: Proportion of HPCIA prescriptions with a culture result or pick-list reason entered
outcomes.why: Separates a failed idea from a prompt that is clicked through.

outcomes.name: Amoxicillin-clavulanate share
outcomes.measure: Weekly amoxicillin-clavulanate prescriptions divided by all systemic antimicrobial prescriptions
outcomes.why: Substitution towards another broad-spectrum drug would hide a shift rather than better prescribing.

outcomes.name: Re-consultation within 7 days
outcomes.measure: Proportion of consultations for diarrhoea or lower urinary tract signs followed by a re-consultation for the same problem within 7 days
outcomes.why: Animals left untreated or given a narrower drug must not do worse.

outcomes.name: Owner complaints about prescribing
outcomes.measure: Count of complaints mentioning antimicrobials or injections logged by reception
outcomes.why: Owner acceptance is part of whether the change can last.

feasibility: About 15 minutes a week of practice manager time for the report, about two hours a month of head nurse time for sampling, the approved 20-minute monthly feedback slot and one prompt configured by the software administrator.
biasMitigation: Fixed list of HPCIA products and a written operational definition before the baseline is extracted
Same report run every Monday by the same person
Random selection of sampled urinary consultations from the week's list
Annotated run chart recording cycle changes, staffing changes and outside campaigns

biasFlags.label: Secular and seasonal change
biasFlags.note: Compare with the same months last year and annotate the chart.

biasFlags.label: Coding drift in the report
biasFlags.note: Drug-class extraction does not depend on coded reasons.

flags: Two process and three balancing measures; no effect claims beyond the aim
parsimony.simplestPath: One outcome measure from an existing report, four short cycles, existing meetings and staff.

theoreticalFramework: Model for Improvement with PDSA cycles; no additional framework is needed.
summary: Four PDSA cycles after a 12-week retrospective baseline; one outcome measure, two process and three balancing measures.
